clue.text: See 15
Flower briefly seen in borders of rockery

indicators.note: these words say the two-word name, written briefly, shows at the outer edges of the following word

parts.note: the outer letters of rockery are R and Y: R is the usual short form of the first word, and Y is the letter whose name is spelt W-Y-E

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a flower peeping out at the edges of a rock garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: something that flows. Shorten the two words to R and Y and you find them at the edges of rockery. The Wye flows along the England–Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is anything that flows, and the Wye is a British river.

clue.text: Wear shirt unbuttoned? Journalist material

indicators.note: a shirt worn unbuttoned is loose and dishevelled, so the letters of wear shirt are thrown into disorder

parts.note: ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A dress tip: wear your shirt open, says a fashion journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbuttoned?' is the anagram signal: an open shirt hangs loose. The cloth is a woollen fabric from the Outer Hebrides, and the answer spans two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A woollen cloth hand-woven in the Outer Hebrides is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Sick notes daughter produces at inopportune moment

parts.note: sick means ill
to time something is to note how long it takes, so notes stands for time
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A daughter turns up with a sick note at a bad moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' is the loosest piece: as a verb, timing a race is noting its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Something badly timed happens when the occasion is unsuitable.

clue.text: Lead-free substance akin to vapour trail, leaving one sort of plane

indicators.note: lead here is the leading letter, so lead-free means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a vapour is a kind of gas

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, which leaves the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unleaded fuel produces a vapour trail, an aviation note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' looks like petrol but drops the G from GAS; 'leaving one' takes I out of TRAIL. 'plane' is a level of existence, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Occultists speak of the astral plane, a level of existence beyond the physical.

clue.text: See 21
Complain about this Latin hairstyle

indicators.note: about means the complaining word goes around the Latin word

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a classical-sounding haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mohican is a strip of upright hair over a shaved head (the US 'mohawk').
explanation.definitionFit: The style is named after the Native American people once thought to wear it.

clue.text: First of clues missed out? Puck's hard to find

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are set out in a new order
first of points to the opening letter of the word clues as the one to go
missed means that opening letter is left out

parts.note: Puck is the setter, so Puck's (Puck has) is I'VE from the setter's own mouth

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that, with the first clue missing, he is impossible to pin down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' and 'missed' remove C from CLUES; 'out' rearranges LUES into ELUS; Puck's = I have, I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive evades capture or is difficult to locate.

clue.text: Given in to green-eyed monster?

indicators.note: given in means the letters are contained within the words to green-eyed

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders to jealousy, Shakespeare's green-eyed monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes 'the green-eyed monster', jealousy, in Othello; ogres are often pictured green.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutish giant of folklore is a kind of fearsome creature.

clue.text: One who revels in Irish republic's model meets king and queen

parts.note: ROI is short for Republic of Ireland, with the S of the possessive
the Model T was Ford's famous car
ER stands for Edward Rex, King Edward
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A party-loving Irishman meets royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ERs come from different monarchs: Edward Rex and Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy merrymaker is someone who parties boisterously.

clue.text: Mongoose I see hotel has on menu, surprisingly

parts.note: C sounds like see, a crossword convention
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of on menu are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner is shocked to find mongoose on the hotel menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mongoose was called by this Greek name, meaning 'tracker'.

clue.text: The French hope a poet becomes world champion

parts.note: le is French for the
a wish is a hope
John Milton wrote Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A French hope that a poet will win a world title.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights; it is the British Formula One driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The British racing driver has won the Formula One drivers' title several times.

clue.text: Compare bushy beards and crusty spots, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: lichen grows on rocks and trees as crusty patches or as shaggy, beard-like tufts

explanation.surface: Someone compares a bushy beard to an outbreak of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichen is pronounced LIKE-en by many, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken is to draw a comparison between two things.

clue.text: See 12
Organ stops essentially modulate

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter, of stops

parts.note: to modulate is to vary

explanation.surface: An organist pulls out the stops to change key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'stops' suggest a church organ; the organ is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The female reproductive gland that produces eggs is a body part.

clue.text: Broadcaster got a snob raving about E-number

parts.note: Sky is a UK satellite broadcaster

indicators.note: raving about means the letters of got a snob and E are thrown about madly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV station hears a snob ranting about food additives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E-number' looks like a food additive; 'number' is the definition, a song. The answer spans three lights: a Scottish folk song about Bonnie Prince Charlie's escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, as in a performer's set.

clue.text: See 3
Seasick in Hertfordshire town? That's stunningly shocking!

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London

indicators.note: sick inside the word seasick suggests the letters of sea are churned up

explanation.surface: Someone is seasick in a landlocked English town, which is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasick' must be split into fodder and the anagram signal 'sick'; the result goes 'in' the town. Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser stuns its target with an electric shock, so using one shocks to stun.

clue.text: See 15
African primate, one of two very young ones destined to be president?

definitions.meaning: a small, big-eyed nocturnal galago of Africa

definitions.text: one of two very young ones destined to be president?
definitions.meaning: either George Bush, father or son, as an infant before reaching the White House

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: an infant who would grow up to be a President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A galago, a small leaping nocturnal African primate, has this common name.

clue.text: Mother backed by her brothers in America

parts.note: a mother's brothers are uncles to her children

indicators.note: backed means the word for mother is written backwards

parts.note: ma means mother

explanation.surface: A mother is supported by her brothers in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in the striped hat personifies the US government.

clue.text: Flipping firm behind's covered seat

indicators.note: covered means the reversed firm is enclosed by the word for behind

parts.note: late means behind time

indicators.note: flipping means the firm's abbreviation is turned over, backwards

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An irritated remark about a firm whose seat has a covered behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but reverses CO to OC, which LATE covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To seat a thing is to set or place it somewhere, as to situate it.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, like unfermented grape juice?

definitions.meaning: stale and out of date in outlook
must is unfermented grape juice, so a playful adjective for resembling it adds Y

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: must plus the adjective ending -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale, mouldy and fusty things suggest something antiquated and out of date.

clue.text: Make a mess of Puck's anagram, putting the twelfth letter first

indicators.note: putting with first places the Greek letter at the front of the word
first says the Greek letter goes ahead of the rest

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: anagram signals the setter's name is rearranged

parts.note: Puck is the setter's pseudonym; the anagram is of his name

explanation.surface: The setter invites us to rearrange his name and botch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelfth letter' is unmarked as Greek, which solvers found unfair; 'anagram' rearranges the setter's name and 'putting ... first' sets the Greek letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle something is to ruin it through clumsiness.

clue.text: Pasta originally celebrated in a form of verse

parts.note: macaroni is tube-shaped pasta

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of celebrated

explanation.surface: Pasta celebrated in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaronic verse mixes vernacular words with Latin endings; the name comes from the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic poetry mixing two languages, often Latin with a vernacular, has this name.

clue.text: Consider money needed for parking in Jersey

indicators.note: needed for means money stands in place of parking

parts.note: a jersey is a pullover, a knitted top
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Paying for parking on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the Channel Island but is a sweater. The answer spans two lights.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something is to think it over carefully.

clue.text: Soft drink for a footballer

parts.note: B marks a soft pencil lead
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A footballer orders a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Bale is a Welsh footballer. 'Soft drink' reads as a single phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth Bale played for Real Madrid and Wales.

clue.text: One promoting free movement Tory leader's demoted twice

indicators.note: the leading letter is moved down two places in the word

parts.note: blue is the Conservative party colour, so a Tory is a blue

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader has been demoted twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifting B from first to third turns BLUE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lubricant helps parts slide freely, so it promotes easy movement.

clue.text: Sandwich with a brown filling? That's very obvious

indicators.note: filling means a and the brown word go inside the sandwich

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a sandwich with a brown filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flagrant is open and unconcealed, impossible to miss.

clue.text: Steps taken before beginning to bake a small cake

indicators.note: taken before puts the dance ahead of the rest

parts.note: the rumba is a dance, a set of steps

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of bake

explanation.surface: Instructions to take some steps before baking a little cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup is a dessert pastry.
